narrative: Distilled 2026-08-29 from a reference the platform owner brought (liaisongraphics.com) as the worked example of the RUNWAY language. A one-woman brand-and-web design studio whose clients are beauty entrepreneurs and small creators; she is the face of the work, leads with the craft, sells tiered packages with pay-later, and wants the site to feel like she just walked into the room. Fills library holes: craft_first + proud/ambitious, a soft_dark tonal-monochrome page with expressive display, expressive motion, and the portrait_presence hero on a studio (not a ministry). Resulting direction: THE MAKER IS THE BRAND — black, white and one grey with no accent colour at all; the owner in motion as the hero under a light-weight headline and a star glyph; sections meeting on arcs; the work shown inside device frames on a horizontal strip; one black ribbon repeating the offer. Teaches: face-first hero on a monochrome page, arc seams, device-framed portfolio strip, the offer marquee, and letting the work carry all the colour.

evidence: their three verbs: Brand / Build / Launch
some have had three logos already; some have never hired a designer
they've built something and they want it to look like it
you come to me for the taste; that's the job
they want visitors to feel: she's the one, she's booked, she's worth it
never like: pastel portfolio grids with pink script fonts
the wordmark stays; the rest can change
they asked for a gallery of real work

palette.because: No accent colour at all — black, white, one grey; the client work in the device frames carries every colour on the page (P4: dark stage, the work performs). The pastel convention is refused outright (P10).

typography.pairing_logic: A geometric display at LIGHT weight (300–400) for the welcome line with one star glyph, uppercase wide-tracked section titles in the same family at small size, a plain grotesque body — contrast in weight and tracking, kinship in geometry (P5: expert_above carried by restraint, not heaviness).
typography.because: Swagger in a light weight reads as taste; the same words in bold would read as a gym.

layout.because: P6: the owner on one side of the hero, the welcome on the other; below, the work strip and the offer ribbon run as parallel bands separated by arcs, never straight seams.

motion.signature_move: she walks in — the hero is a short soft-focus reel of the owner moving; the work strip scrolls sideways; the ribbon runs
motion.because: P8/P12: a high-conviction maker gets a page that moves like her, but only in three named places; every other element is still.

hero_concept.concept_statement: The owner in motion — a soft-focus reel or a blurred still — full-bleed in grey; over it, right of centre, WHERE CREATIVITY MEETS STRATEGY in small caps, 'Welcome to the studio ★' in the light display, and LET'S WORK with an arrow. A black band with a rounded top rises from the bottom of the frame.
hero_concept.because: craft_first + expert_above on a person-led studio → the maker is the brand; the face is the proof (P15) and the work is one scroll away.

whitespace.because: Chapters are cut by arcs — black over grey, grey over black — so the scroll reads as a runway of bands, not a stack of sections.

notes: 'let's work' is the only CTA copy on the page, repeated as a white pill with an arrow
the work is shown inside device frames — phone, laptop, business card — on a horizontal strip the visitor scrolls sideways
the three packages sit on the grey band as three hairline columns with BRAND NOW › PAY LATER running as a black ribbon above them
section titles are uppercase, wide-tracked and centred; body copy is two sentences max
voice_to_visual.because: A short second-person voice with swagger becomes a page of bands, frames and one repeated command.

rule_break.what: the hero is a soft-focus reel of the designer herself, not the work — on a portfolio site
rule_break.because: Every design studio leads with the work; leading with the maker in motion is the one loud break, and the work follows one scroll later in frames.

tension.expression: Presence owns the hero reel, the light display, the arcs; the work owns every colour on the page, the device-framed strip and the packages — the monochrome page is what lets both hold.
tension.because: All maker reads as vanity; all work reads as a template gallery — the black-and-white page seats them together.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: She just walked in, and she's the one.
first_impression.remember: Her, moving, in grey — and the work in frames sliding past underneath.
first_impression.because: legit_intentional for a proud ambitious client = a maker who looks booked.

language.because: A designer who is the face of the work, with real portfolio pieces, bold conviction and a refusal of the pastel convention — face first, work second, black and white so the work carries the colour; Monograph would gild what wants to be stark.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Shares the asymmetric balanced dark-ish stage and the expressive display face with e6, but is tonal (no accent), soft-dark, expressive in motion and led by a portrait; shares the portrait hero and soft-dark ground with e12 on the opposite temperature and pace.

summary_for_practitioner: Your site opens with you — a soft-focus reel of you moving, in grey, with 'Welcome to the studio ★' in a light typeface and LET'S WORK beside it. The whole page is black, white and one grey; the only colour comes from your clients' work, shown inside phone and laptop frames on a strip you scroll sideways. Sections meet on curves, not straight lines. Your three packages sit on the grey band under a black ribbon that runs BRAND NOW › PAY LATER across the page, and every button on the site is the same white pill with an arrow.
